video.title: The ChatGPT Scam That's Too Good to Be True: Don't Get Caught!

summary: A short promotional teaser warning that people searching how to make money with ChatGPT are being targeted by malware, fake apps and fake browser extensions that steal ChatGPT logins. The speaker cites over 101,000 infected devices and about 27,000 credential sets sold on the dark web in a month. Stolen chat histories can expose business ideas, financial numbers and client details. The key takeaway is to verify the legitimacy of any AI opportunity or app before using it, and the full episode (linked in the description) covers what to check in your own ChatGPT account.

warnings.warning: Fake apps and fake browser extensions impersonating ChatGPT can install malware that steals logins; OpenAI itself was not hacked, the users were.

quote.text: OpenAI, yeah, they were never hacked. The users were hacked. Fake apps, fake browser extensions, one click, all dressed up to look like the real thing.
quote.speaker: Host

warnings.warning: A stolen AI login exposes saved conversation history, including business ideas, financial numbers, client details and personal details.

quote.text: By default it saves the conversation history. So a stolen login doesn't just give a scammer a tool, it gives them your entire playbook
quote.speaker: Host

warnings.warning: Searching for 'make money with ChatGPT' opportunities can lead to malware-laden fake offers; check the legitimacy of any AI opportunity before engaging.

quote.text: Before you chase an AI opportunity, check the door that you're about to walk through.
quote.speaker: Host

warnings.warning: Investment scams approached via messaging apps such as WhatsApp can cause catastrophic losses.

quote.text: A bank CEO in Kansas met a fake investment advisor on WhatsApp and lost his savings, then his daughter's college fund
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Treat AI accounts as sensitive assets: chat history can hold business plans, financials and client data, so protect logins and review account security and history settings.

quote.text: Think about what you actually type into ChatGPT or Claude or any of the other AIs. Business ideas, financial numbers, client details, personal details.
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Only install AI apps and browser extensions from verified official sources, as lookalikes are the main attack vector.

quote.text: the smartest move isn't really avoiding AI, it's knowing the difference between the real front door and the trap door
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Scammers exploit human trust rather than technical weaknesses, so scepticism toward unsolicited opportunities is the main defence.

quote.text: The scammers don't need outsmart ChatGPT, they just need outsmart you.
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Do not put client confidential or sensitive data into AI tools without considering account security, especially in a UK business subject to GDPR obligations.
Fear-based hooks in short teasers drive traffic to a longer episode; treat statistics cited without named sources with caution.

evidence_quality.rationale: A 2-minute promotional teaser with no business idea. Statistics are attributed to an unnamed cybersecurity firm and are second-hand and unverified. Useful only as a general security warning.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Teaser drives viewers to the full episode linked in the description; the channel sells entrepreneurship content.
